title: Trump at the UN: Accuses Mexico of Being the “Epicenter” of Drug Trafficking, but Highlights Progress with Its Government
author: Jim Cason and David Brooks
content:
_This article by[Jim Cason and David
Brooks](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Jim%20Cason%20y%20David%20Brooks,%20corresponsales)
originally appeared in the [September 22, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/09/22/mundo/trump-en-la-onu-
mexico-epicentro-de-la-violencia-de-los-carteles-debe-recuperar-el-control-de-
manos-de-los-enemigos-de-la-humanidad), Mexico's premier left wing daily
newspaper._

**Washington and New York**. President Donald Trump reiterated in his speech
before the [United
Nations](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/09/22/mundo/en-medio-de-
pasarela-en-la-onu-medios-boicotean-actos-de-trump-por-vetar-a-periodistas)
that Mexico is “the epicenter” of drug cartel violence in Latin America, that
the Mexican government has ceded control of its territory to the cartels and,
shortly afterward, his White House warned that **if Mexico does not take
action to confront this, the United States will be forced to do so** (without
defining exactly what it would do).

> It is unacceptable for the United States to share a 2,000-mile border with a
> territory controlled by the cartels. Mexico has to take back control of its
> land from the enemies of humanity.
>
> Donald Trump, before the UN General Assembly

The president repeated his “unprecedented” successes in the fight against
drugs, declaring that the cartels are **“the ISIS of the Western Hemisphere”**
whose members must be treated as “terrorists,” and stated that Mexico “is the
epicenter of cartel violence.”

Perhaps seeking to soften the impact of his message, he emphasized that “I am
proud to tell you that we have **a very good relationship with the Mexican
government**. We have taken great steps, very great steps, with Mexico. They
don’t want the cartels either. And when that day comes, the whole region will
be a better, safer and more beautiful place in which to live and prosper.”

Although Trump frequently improvises during his speeches, including occasions
when he has voiced criticisms of Mexico that were not in his prepared text,
his words today included very specific phrases designed to increase the
pressure on the Mexican government. Less than an hour after his speech before
the UN, the White House “drug czar” Sara Carter offered more details about
what her government wants from the Mexican government in this area.

“I think the United States is working very closely with our Mexican
counterparts, and I know that,” Carter commented in a social media message
this morning. “If there are politicians who are working with the cartels,
whether in Mexico or even in the United States, if we find out about it **we
will go after them and hold them accountable** for it.”

She added that “this is a very important part of what our government is doing.
President Donald Trump has made it very clear that our government will no
longer sit back and allow these cartels to operate with impunity. Part of that
is holding accountable the people who are working with the cartels.”
